html:
Killing of hundreds of unarmed Vietnamese villagers by American soldiers at My Lai, in Quang Ngai province, on 16 March 1968, during the Vietnam War.

Charlie Company of the US Army's Americal Division was sent in after heavy losses and told the village was a Viet Cong base. No enemy fire met them. Soldiers shot women, children and old men, and raped and burned. The US Army counts 347 dead, a Vietnamese memorial 504. Lieutenant William Calley led the platoon. Helicopter pilot Hugh Thompson landed between soldiers and villagers and saved some.

The army covered it up for over a year. In March 1969 a former soldier, Ron Ridenhour, wrote letters to officials and Congress about what he had heard. Reporter Seymour Hersh broke the story in November 1969, and photographs followed.

Calley was convicted in the 1971 trial, the only one. The case turned many Americans against the war.
sum: Killing of hundreds of unarmed Vietnamese villagers by American soldiers at My Lai, in Quang Ngai province, on 16 March 1968, during the Vietnam War.
